zh.title: 空中巴士A321XLR增重換航程 為何不到1小時短程航線也照飛
zh.summary: 空中巴士A321XLR最大起飛重量達101.5噸，比A321neo重4.5噸，換來4,700浬航程；但加航與愛爾蘭航空等業者仍把它排上不到1小時的短程航線，因為機隊共通性與飛機利用率，比單純的重量代價更重要。
body: 空中巴士A321XLR是目前航程最長的窄體客機，最大起飛重量101.5噸，比標準A321neo的97噸重4.5噸，航程則由4,000浬增至4,700浬。兩者外觀幾乎相同，座位數、機身尺寸與發動機選擇都一樣，差別在於XLR加裝了容量12,900公升的永久後中央油箱，並更新燃油系統與結構補強，換來更長的航程。

儘管XLR是為長程瘦航線而生，不少業者卻把它排上短程航線。加航以XLR飛渥太華—多倫多，約39分鐘、197浬，也飛蒙特婁—多倫多，約53分鐘、274浬；愛爾蘭航空今年7月飛了300多班超過3,100英里的XLR航班，同時也有200多班在1,250英里以下，包括都柏林—倫敦希斯羅僅48分鐘、都柏林—巴塞隆納1小時50分鐘。截至11月中，XLR已交付61架給11家業者，訂單逾500架，伊比利亞航空2024年10月首家接收，現有8架。
業者接受重量代價的原因，在於XLR與A321neo尺寸相同，可共用登機門間距與地面設備，機組也不需另取型別檢定，加上飛機停在地面就不賺錢，排上短程航線仍比閒置划算。伊比利亞執行長曾表示，XLR的航程表現比原先預期更好，已能飛往加勒比海的聖胡安與聖多明哥；反觀加航原定以XLR飛多倫多—倫敦希斯羅，卻在首航前撤換，顯示排班仍需配合實際營運需求。

en.title: Why airlines accept the Airbus A321XLR's heavier 101.5-tonne takeoff weight on sub-hour flights
en.summary: The Airbus A321XLR's maximum takeoff weight of 101.5 tonnes is 4.5 tonnes heavier than the A321neo's, buying 4,700 nautical miles of range — yet Air Canada, Aer Lingus and other operators still schedule it on flights of under an hour, because fleet commonality and keeping the aircraft earning matter more than the weight penalty.
body: The Airbus A321XLR is the longest-range commercial narrowbody, with a maximum takeoff weight of 101.50 tonnes (222,667 pounds) against 97.00 tonnes (213,848 pounds) for the standard A321neo, and a range of 4,700 nautical miles (8,700 km) against 4,000 nautical miles (7,400 km). The two types look almost identical, with the same 244-seat maximum capacity, the same dimensions and the same CFM LEAP-1A or Pratt & Whitney PW1100G engines; the XLR's extra range comes mainly from a permanent 12,900-litre rear centre tank, an updated fuel system and structural reinforcements.

Despite being built for long, thin routes, the XLR regularly appears on short hops. Air Canada flies it between Ottawa and Toronto in about 39 minutes (197 nautical miles) and between Montreal and Toronto in about 53 minutes (274 nautical miles), while also using it on the almost nine-hour Toronto-Tenerife route. In July, Aer Lingus flew more than 300 XLR flights over 3,100 miles and more than 200 of 1,250 miles or fewer, including Dublin-London Heathrow at 48 minutes and Dublin-Barcelona at one hour and 50 minutes. As of mid-November, 61 XLRs had been delivered to 11 carriers out of more than 500 orders, with Iberia — the launch customer in October 2024 — operating eight.

Airlines accept the weight penalty because the XLR shares the A321neo's dimensions, so the same gate spacing and ground equipment can be used and pilots can fly either variant without a separate type rating, and because an aircraft on the ground earns nothing. Iberia chief executive Marco Antonio Trujillo said the XLR was "even better than originally planned in terms of stage length," noting it now flies to the Caribbean, San Juan and Santo Domingo. Air Canada, by contrast, pulled the type from a planned Toronto-London Heathrow service before it could debut, a reminder that advance planning still has to meet real-time operational needs.
